notes: Summary: Mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood for embeddings + semantic search. Primary driver: replace a brittle in-house vector pipeline and reduce per-search latency/cost. They ran a hosted-API POC first and are now sizing Dedicated for production. Key numbers: target P95 latency <= 80ms for in-app search, steady-state throughput 200-300 qps with peaks to 500 qps, daily batch ingest ~10M vectors (delta + full reindexes overnight). Current stack: Postgres + S3 for docs, Pinecone for vector store (pilot), Airflow for batch jobs. They used Redwood hosted embeddings during POC and saw decent quality but cost creep at scale — interested in Dedicated to get predictable unit economics and autoscaling for nightly batch windows. Technical asks: vector DB connector patterns (Pinecone vs self-hosted FAISS/Annoy), support for incremental reindexing, KV cache behavior for short-context reranking, streaming responses not necessary for current use case. Security: must pass SOC2 + SSO/SAML + KMS integration; retention controls and audit logs required for enterprise customers. Quote from Head of Product: "We need sub-100ms, predictable pricing, and a simple way to do nightly 10M vector ingests without blowing cloud spend." Commercial notes: interested in a 6–12 month committed Dedicated pilot with option to expand; ARR target band $50k–$150k. Next steps: finalize Dedicated pilot sizing, provide a scoped SOW and SLA, deliver security artifacts (SOC2 + KMS design), and run a 2-week dedicated performance validation (latency + throughput) using customer's vector DB or Redwood-managed store. Open questions: exact cost delta between RDW-hosted embeddings vs Dedicated quantized model; support window and runbook for large nightly reindexes; recommended backfill strategy and expected downtime during migration.
